tip.winamax: Tournaments: you need the hand history file (HH) + the summary (_summary.txt). Cash game: the hand history file is enough. You can drop a whole folder — NutsIQ detects and sorts files automatically.

1.title: Open Winamax settings
1.text: From the Winamax lobby, click the ⚙ icon (gear) in the right sidebar.

2.title: Go to "Tracker"
2.text: In the left menu, scroll down and click Tracker.

3.title: Open the history folder
3.text: In "Hand history location", click OPEN to reveal the folder on your computer.

4.title: Drop the "history" folder
4.text: In the folder that opens: winamax > documents > accounts > <your name> > history. Drop the whole folder (or the .txt files) into NutsIQ.

1.title: Sign in to your player area
1.text: On the Betclic website, go to the Poker section of your account.

2.title: Download your hand history
2.text: Go to Poker → Hand History and export your hands as .txt.

3.title: Drop the files into NutsIQ
3.text: Drop the downloaded .txt files directly into the zone above.

leaks.method: References version {{version}}: online MTTs from €5 to €20, solid regulars, hands with 15 BB or more. A leak is confirmed only when the whole 95 % confidence interval is outside the reference.

tooHigh.title: You play too many hands
tooHigh.why: You enter {{rate}} of pots (reference {{min}}–{{max}}). Too many weak hands end up out of position or dominated after the flop.
tooHigh.work: Tighten your opening and calling ranges, especially early and against raises.

tooLow.title: You play too few hands
tooLow.why: You enter {{rate}} of pots (reference {{min}}–{{max}}). You give up blinds and antes that are easy to win.
tooLow.work: Open wider in late position and defend your big blind more.

tooHigh.title: You raise too often
tooHigh.why: You raise {{rate}} of hands (reference {{min}}–{{max}}). Your raises become easy to re-raise.
tooHigh.work: Keep raises for hands and positions that justify them.

tooLow.title: You do not raise enough
tooLow.why: You raise {{rate}} of hands (reference {{min}}–{{max}}). Without the initiative you win fewer pots without a showdown.
tooLow.work: Enter pots by raising rather than calling, especially when nobody has bet yet.

tooHigh.title: You call much more than you raise
tooHigh.why: {{rate}} of hands are played by calling only (reference up to {{max}}). Calling hands the initiative to opponents.
tooHigh.work: Turn some of your preflop calls into raises or folds.

tooLow.title: Unusual VPIP/PFR gap
tooLow.why: The gap between hands played and hands raised is {{rate}} (reference {{min}}–{{max}}).
tooLow.work: Check that you defend your blinds enough by calling.

tooHigh.title: You open too wide from {{position}}
tooHigh.why: You open {{rate}} of the times it is folded to you in {{position}} (reference {{min}}–{{max}}).
tooHigh.work: Drop the weakest hands from your opening range in that position.

tooLow.title: You open too little from {{position}}
tooLow.why: You open {{rate}} of the times it is folded to you in {{position}} (reference {{min}}–{{max}}). These are profitable pots you leave.
tooLow.work: Add playable hands (small pairs, suited connectors, suited aces) to your range in that position.

tooHigh.title: You limp too much
tooHigh.why: You enter by calling {{rate}} of the times it is folded to you (reference up to {{max}}). In MTTs, limping leads to multiway pots out of position.
tooHigh.work: When nobody has entered, raise or fold.

tooHigh.title: You steal too much
tooHigh.why: You open {{rate}} of the times it is folded to you in the cutoff, button or small blind (reference {{min}}–{{max}}). The blinds will start re-raising you.
tooHigh.work: Keep a stealing range you can defend against a re-raise.

tooLow.title: You do not steal the blinds enough
tooLow.why: You open {{rate}} of the times it is folded to you in the cutoff, button or small blind (reference {{min}}–{{max}}). Antes make these steals very profitable in tournaments.
tooLow.work: Open more often in late position when it is folded to you.

tooHigh.title: You 3-bet too much
tooHigh.why: You 3-bet {{rate}} of the times you face a raise (reference {{min}}–{{max}}).
tooHigh.work: Keep 3-bets for your best hands and a few well-chosen bluffs.

tooLow.title: You do not 3-bet enough
tooLow.why: You 3-bet {{rate}} of the times you face a raise (reference {{min}}–{{max}}). Opponents open without fear.
tooLow.work: Re-raise your strong hands instead of calling, and add a few bluffs in position.

tooHigh.title: You fold too much to 3-bets
tooHigh.why: You fold {{rate}} of your opens to a re-raise (reference {{min}}–{{max}}). You can be re-raised with anything.
tooHigh.work: Defend more: call in position or 4-bet your best hands.

tooLow.title: You do not fold enough to 3-bets
tooLow.why: You fold only {{rate}} of your opens to a re-raise (reference {{min}}–{{max}}).
tooLow.work: Open hands that can continue, and let the others go against a 3-bet.

tooHigh.title: You c-bet the flop too much
tooHigh.why: You bet {{rate}} of flops as the preflop raiser (reference {{min}}–{{max}}).
tooHigh.work: Check more on flops that hit your opponent's range.

tooLow.title: You do not c-bet the flop enough
tooLow.why: You bet {{rate}} of flops as the preflop raiser (reference {{min}}–{{max}}). You give up the initiative too soon.
tooLow.work: Bet small more often on flops that favour your range.

tooHigh.title: You go to showdown too often
tooHigh.why: You reach showdown in {{rate}} of the flops you see (reference {{min}}–{{max}}). You call down too many medium hands.
tooHigh.work: Let go of more medium hands against strong turn and river pressure.

tooLow.title: You give up too often after the flop
tooLow.why: You reach showdown in {{rate}} of the flops you see (reference {{min}}–{{max}}). You are too easy to push off a hand.
tooLow.work: Defend your medium hands more against single bets.

tooHigh.title: You win a lot at showdown
tooHigh.why: You win {{rate}} of showdowns (reference {{min}}–{{max}}): often a sign you only get there with very strong hands.
tooHigh.work: Check you are not folding too many medium hands earlier.

tooLow.title: You lose too much at showdown
tooLow.why: You win {{rate}} of showdowns (reference {{min}}–{{max}}). You go too far with beaten hands.
tooLow.work: Review your river calls: a medium hand facing a big bet is often beaten.

tooHigh.title: You give up too often to c-bets
tooHigh.why: You fold {{rate}} of the time to the preflop raiser's flop bet (reference {{min}}–{{max}}). He can bet his whole range at a profit.
tooHigh.work: Call more often with draws and weak pairs on dry flops, especially against small bets.

tooLow.title: You do not give up enough to c-bets
tooLow.why: You only fold {{rate}} of the time to the preflop raiser's flop bet (reference {{min}}–{{max}}). You call with too many hands going nowhere.
tooLow.work: Fold high cards without a draw when the flop favours the raiser.

tooHigh.title: You fire the second barrel too often
tooHigh.why: You bet {{rate}} of turns after a called c-bet (reference {{min}}–{{max}}). Your bluffs get expensive against players who call.
tooHigh.work: Keep the second barrel for made hands, draws and cards that favour you.

tooLow.title: You give up on the turn too quickly
tooLow.why: You only bet {{rate}} of turns after a called c-bet (reference {{min}}–{{max}}). Players can call the flop and take the pot from you.
tooLow.work: Keep betting on cards that help your range (aces, kings, flush cards) and with your draws.

tooHigh.title: You check-raise too often
tooHigh.why: You raise {{rate}} of flop bets after checking (reference {{min}}–{{max}}). Too many chips go in with medium hands.
tooHigh.work: Keep the check-raise for strong hands and good draws.

tooLow.title: You almost never check-raise
tooLow.why: You only raise {{rate}} of flop bets after checking (reference {{min}}–{{max}}). Players can bet into you without risk.
tooLow.work: Add check-raises with sets, two pair and strong draws, especially from the big blind.

tooHigh.title: You win many pots after the flop
tooHigh.why: You win {{rate}} of the pots where you see the flop (reference {{min}}–{{max}}). If you see few flops, you may be too tight before.
tooHigh.work: Nothing urgent: check you do not fold too many playable hands preflop.

tooLow.title: You win few pots after the flop
tooLow.why: You only win {{rate}} of the pots where you see the flop (reference {{min}}–{{max}}). You see too many flops with weak hands, or give up too soon.
tooLow.work: See fewer flops out of position and bet more often when shown weakness.

tooHigh.title: You are very aggressive after the flop
tooHigh.why: {{rate}} of your decisions after the flop are bets or raises (reference {{min}}–{{max}}). Good players will let you bluff.
tooHigh.work: Call more with medium hands instead of turning them into bluffs.

tooLow.title: You are too passive after the flop
tooLow.why: Only {{rate}} of your decisions after the flop are bets or raises (reference {{min}}–{{max}}). Calling instead of betting gives up fold equity.
tooLow.work: Bet strong hands for value and draws as semi-bluffs instead of calling.

sizing.questionThreeBet: {{opener}} opens to {{open}}. You 3-bet {{hand}} from {{position}}, {{stack}} effective: to how much?

verdict.method: Sizing references v{{version}} (low-stakes MTTs with antes, no ICM): our conventions, not GTO.

rules.open: Above 25 BB, a small raise is enough (2 to 2.3 BB, up to 2.5 BB deep): with antes the pot is already big, and raising more risks more to steal the same.
rules.openShort: Between 15 and 25 BB, min-raise (2 BB): the raise is cheap and lets you fold without regret to an all-in 3-bet.
rules.openSmallBlind: From the small blind, raise bigger (2.5 BB below 25 BB, 3 BB above): you will play the hand out of position, so make the big blind pay to see the flop.
rules.threeBetIp: In position, about 3 times the open: you will play the rest of the hand in position, no need to inflate the pot.
rules.threeBetOop: Out of position, about 4 times the open: a bigger raise makes the opener pay for his positional edge and cuts his calls.
rules.threeBetShort: Below 25 BB effective ({{stack}} here), the 3-bet is a shove: a smaller raise would commit you anyway without taking all the fold equity.
rules.threeBetCommit: At {{stack}} effective, a 3-bet to {{multiple}} would put more than a third of your stack in: you would be committed, so shove straight away.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.heading: Privacy
privacy.intro: What NutsIQ keeps about you, why, and how to erase all of it.

controller.title: Who is responsible
controller.body: NutsIQ is an independent project, being tested by a small group of players. Its publisher is the controller of your data.

data.title: What we keep
data.body: Your Google identifier, or your email address and password (stored only as an irreversible hash, never in clear), your display name and language. The hand histories and tournament summaries you import, as they are (they contain the screen names of the players at your tables), and everything we compute from them: statistics, leaks, weekly plans. The bankroll movements you enter and your training answers.

purposes.title: Why
purposes.body: Only to provide the service: analyse your game and follow your progress. We also count which features each account opens every day, to learn what is actually useful. Nothing is sold, shared for advertising or used for marketing.

ai.title: AI coach
ai.body: When you ask for a leak explanation, a tournament debrief or a weekly review, the figures computed by NutsIQ and, when needed, example hands are sent to Anthropic, our AI provider, in anonymised form: positions, actions and amounts, without your screen name, your opponents' or the tournament's name. Anthropic processes this data in the United States on our behalf. The texts written are kept with your account and included in your export.

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.body: Only the cookies the app needs to work: your session, form protection and the round trip through Google at sign-in. No advertising cookies and no third-party analytics, hence no banner.

hosting.title: Hosting
hosting.body: The app and its database are hosted in France (Paris) by Scaleway. Opponents' screen names in your files never leave our servers. Account emails (confirmation, password) are sent by Brevo, a provider hosted in the European Union.

retention.title: How long we keep it
retention.body: Your data is kept as long as your account exists. Feature usage is erased after 13 months. When you delete your account, everything is erased at once; backups holding a copy expire on their own within 30 days.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.body: From the Account page you can download all your data (your original files included) and delete your account, without asking anyone. You can also ask for inaccurate data to be corrected or object to a processing.

contact.title: Contact
contact.email: For any question about your data, write to
contact.account: To export or delete your data, use the Account page once signed in.
contact.authority: You may also lodge a complaint with your data protection authority (in France, the CNIL: cnil.fr).
